seoTitle: Fluent Forms & FluentCRM: Free Newsletter Signup
metaDescription: Build a free email signup form in WordPress using Fluent Forms, connect it to FluentCRM, and start collecting subscribers without paid tools.
intro: Building a working newsletter signup form usually means paying for a form plugin or email tool, but Fluent Forms and FluentCRM let you do it entirely for free. This guide walks through installing both plugins, creating your form, and connecting new subscribers straight into your email list.

steps.heading: Install and set up Fluent Forms
steps.body: Install the free Fluent Forms plugin from the WordPress repository and complete its basic setup to start building forms.

steps.heading: Create a newsletter signup form
steps.body: Use Fluent Forms' drag-and-drop builder to create a simple email signup form with the fields you want to collect.

steps.heading: Connect Fluent Forms with FluentCRM
steps.body: Set up the integration between Fluent Forms and FluentCRM so every new submission automatically adds the subscriber to your CRM.

steps.heading: Embed the form on your site
steps.body: Add the form to a page or post using the shortcode or block Fluent Forms provides, so visitors can subscribe directly.

steps.heading: Test the signup flow
steps.body: Submit a test entry to confirm the subscriber appears correctly in FluentCRM before promoting the form publicly.

faq.question: Is Fluent Forms really free to use?
faq.answer: Yes, Fluent Forms has a free version available in the WordPress plugin repository that covers basic form building and integrations.

faq.question: Do I need Elementor Pro to use this setup?
faq.answer: No, Fluent Forms can be embedded on any WordPress page using its own shortcode or block, without needing a premium page builder.

faq.question: What does FluentCRM do with the collected emails?
faq.answer: FluentCRM stores and organizes your subscribers so you can send email campaigns and automations directly from WordPress.

faq.question: Why isn't my newsletter signup form working?
faq.answer: Check that the Fluent Forms to FluentCRM integration is properly connected and that the form's shortcode or block was embedded correctly on the page.
